fixed.before: 2v.16–17 seem garbled: under anderhalp is read as unde anderhalp, 'and on the other side'; schoz is unclear (perhaps the swelling or diseased matter). bunge is probably brooklime (Veronica beccabunga). ôrgemint may be orpiment. halgalia is probably galangal. harz bech may be a single item, 'resin-pitch'.
fixed.after: 2v.16–17 seem garbled: under anderhalp is read as unde anderhalp, 'and on the other side'; schoz is the shot, the arrowhead or missile lodged in the wound. bunge is probably brooklime (Veronica beccabunga). ôrgemint may be orpiment. halgalia is probably galangal. harz bech may be a single item, 'resin-pitch'.

fixed.before: Ivie riffe is kept as a word of power; 'hin vile michel' is taken as 'away, very great one', but may itself be a formula. veimen (148v.5) is 'skim off'; its sense here is uncertain. 'daz uns ze lüppe' (148v.6) is obscure (lüppe is 'poison, witchcraft') and seems incomplete. 'ûf harte' may be 'on the wooded hill'; 'engelen dû jagetes' (you hunted angels) is odd; the negative in '[no] more' is supplied. Pat̄ and Pater are taken as the Our Father; 'Mm.' is unexplained.
fixed.after: Ivie riffe is kept as a word of power; 'hin vile michel' is taken as 'away, very great one', but may itself be a formula. veimen (148v.5) is 'skim off'; its sense here is uncertain. 'daz uns ze lüppe' (148v.6) is obscure (lüppe is 'poison, witchcraft') and seems incomplete; it may also mean 'may this serve us as a charm'. 'ûf harte' may be 'on the wooded hill'; 'engelen dû jagetes' (you hunted angels) is odd; the negative in '[no] more' is supplied. Pat̄ and Pater are taken as the Our Father; 'Mm.' is unexplained.

not_upheld.m2#5: geblæsede is from blâsen, 'blow, breathe': 'with frequent panting' is a defensible reading of the phrenitic's symptom.
not_upheld.m1#2: The translator read büechînen bluot as written, 'beech blossom', and gives the dried goat's blood of the stone remedy as the alternative in the note: a marked reading, not an error.
not_upheld.m1#4: dâse is dâ se, 'there ... them'; the insult is the next line, übeliu hornblâse.
not_upheld.m4#3: enwolten ... dunken is 'would ... seem': 'this would not seem enough to Lucifer' accounts for both lines 234-235; the objection leaves 'Lucifern dunken genuoc' unattached.
